root_idea.summary: The root has three lexically distinct orientations: an internal bodily organ or region, deceptive or enchant­ing action, and the time immediately before dawn.
root_idea.development: Classical analysis keeps the bodily, deceptive, and temporal branches distinct. The deceptive branch is described through turning something from its proper appearance or course, while related extensions include subtle influence, fascination, and delusion.

senses.definition: To turn someone or something away from its proper course, state, or manner of being.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic passive use can describe being turned aside from sound judgment or proper apprehension.

senses.definition: To enchant, fascinate, or deceive by making what is false appear true or by making a thing seem other than it is.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes the construction of enchanting or fascinating the eye and the related sense of deluding someone through an apparent illusion.

senses.definition: One endowed with a sahr, that is, a bodily interior or human constitution; hence, a human being subject to bodily needs such as food and drink.
senses.usage_conditions: This Quranic interpretation contrasts human physical dependence with claims of superhuman status.

senses.definition: Repeatedly enchanted, deceived, or deluded so that perception or reason is overcome.
senses.usage_conditions: The intensive passive form can carry the sense of repeated or extensive enchantment, rather than merely a single act.

senses.definition: Bewitched, fascinated, or affected by an enchantment so as to be diverted from ordinary perception or understanding.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in Quranic accusations that a messenger or other person is under an enchantment or is not apprehending matters normally.

senses.definition: Regarded as a human being endowed with a sahr and therefore dependent on food and other bodily needs.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic interpretive reading that emphasizes human constitution rather than magical affliction; it is especially relevant where eating and bodily limitation are at issue.

senses.definition: The time immediately before daybreak; the final part of the night as dawn approaches.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural is أَسْحَارٌ. Quranic usage includes the pre-dawn period generally, without requiring one particular minute or subdivision of the night.

senses.definition: A magician or enchanter, especially one characterized by intensive or repeated practice.
senses.usage_conditions: The intensive pattern presents the agent as habitual or emphatic, while retaining the agentive meaning of ساحر.

senses.definition: A magician, enchanter, or practitioner of sihr.
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle is used for an individual or group alleged to produce enchantment, fascination, or deceptive appearances.

senses.definition: Enchantment, illusion, or deceptive manipulation that makes falsehood appear as truth or causes things to seem other than they are.
senses.usage_conditions: This includes fascination, visual illusion, and subtle operations whose real manner is hidden. It is the principal sense in Quranic accusations that a sign, message, or performance is magic.

senses.definition: Magic practiced through an appeal to or alliance with devils.
senses.usage_conditions: This Quranic usage concerns the teaching or practice of magic associated with satanic assistance, rather than merely persuasive eloquence or an unexplained subtle effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lungs or inner upper-belly region adjoining the throat and windpipe; by extension, the heart, liver, or inner region of the heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Variant vocalizations and related forms are reported; the term can refer broadly to the internal organs attached to the upper digestive and respiratory region.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or hurt someone's lungs, heart, or inner bodily region.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the bodily, non-enchantment verb associated with سَحْرٌ or سُحْرَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have the lungs swell from fear; to be cowardly or, according to one explanation, to exceed one's proper bounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiom اِنتفخ سَحْرُهُ; the cowardice interpretation is distinguished from the disputed explanation involving excess.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet in the expression for a hare whose lungs are said to burst through the speed of its running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic or auspicious appellation, not a general meaning of the anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hope cut off; despair, or something of which one has despaired.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in idioms such as اِنتقطع منه سَحْرِي and صُرِمَ سَحْرُهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The healed scar of a gall on a camel's back, with the place becoming white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nomadic and animal-related noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The uppermost or farthest part of a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same expression can extend to the extremity of land or another thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn someone from one disposition to another, such as from hatred to love.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized extension of turning or diverting, illustrated by a change in emotional orientation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To divert someone from hunger or want by giving food or drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction سَحَرَهُ بِالطَّعَامِ describes feeding and distracting someone so that the immediate want is relieved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gild silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative use recorded for the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Corruption, spoiling, or marring; to spoil clay, earth, or dust so that it is no longer fit for use.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This branch treats سِحْرٌ as equivalent to فساد and is distinct from enchantment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause sheep's or goats' milk to descend before parturition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized physiological usage connected with the adhesion of the lungs to the side through thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away, remove to a distance, or travel far.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an intransitive movement meaning, distinct from turning someone or something aside.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go forth early in the morning, between daybreak prayer and sunrise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is related to the pre-dawn time noun but denotes the act of setting out at that time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give another person or group the pre-dawn meal called سَحُور.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Form II use is causative or transitive: it means supplying the meal, not eating it oneself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become in the pre-dawn period, or to travel or set out during it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb denotes being or moving at the time called سَحَر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat or drink the pre-dawn meal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be food, a meal, parched grain preparation, or milk consumed at سَحَر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a cock to crow, or for a bird to sing or utter its voice, at pre-dawn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form VIII/X-type usage tied to the time noun سَحَر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A purported operation said to change forms or natures, such as making a human being into an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is reported as a claim attributed to non-Arab or popular belief and is explicitly characterized as having no reality by critical authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Powerful or captivating eloquence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression إِنَّ مِنَ البَيَانِ لَسِحْرًا compares persuasive, striking speech to enchantment; the force may be praiseworthy or blameworthy depending on context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Skill, technical knowledge, or science.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This extension can be approving or disapproving; an attested example compares a branch of star knowledge with a branch of enchantment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food, nourishment, or nutriment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained through the subtle or fine effect of nourishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Superabundant rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase غَيْثٌ ذُو سِحْرٍ applies the term to exceptionally plentiful rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whiteness spreading over blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This color term is usually distinguished from the time noun سَحَر, though the forms are homonymous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremity or uppermost part of a desert, land, or other thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A spatial extension associated by the lexical source with the pre-dawn term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The food or drink consumed before dawn, especially the pre-dawn meal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This form names the meal or its food, in contrast with سُحُورٌ, which names the act of eating it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of eating or drinking the pre-dawn meal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun associated especially with تَسَحَّرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having ruptured or painful lungs, or suffering an abdominal complaint attributed to the lungs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is also used of a person with a complaint of the belly arising from lung pain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large in the belly or chest, especially said of a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized physical description, separate from the illness sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow that wounds the lungs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized weapon-related use reported for the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lungs, windpipe, and attached parts of a sheep or goat that a butcher removes and discards.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes the discarded collection of internal parts rather than one single organ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A children's toy that changes apparent color when its attached string is extended in different directions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name extends to things resembling this color-changing plaything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Enchanting, fascinating, or producing a delusive appearance, as of an eye or a mirage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This adjectival use describes an effect or quality, not a person who practices magic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Knowing, skilled, intelligent, or adept.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival extension of the agent noun, distinct from the Quranic accusation of practicing magic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having one's lungs or heart struck or hurt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This literal bodily passive sense is distinct from enchantment and from the Quranic interpretive reading centered on human physical constitution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deprived of reason, or having the intellect corrupted or disordered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive description of mental disturbance, reported independently of the Quranic readings of the form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Spoiled or marred, said of food, herbage, or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The land sense includes ground damaged by excessive rain or by lack of herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having little milk, said of a she-goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description may apply to a goat with a large udder but scant milk.

cautions: The passive participles مُسَحَّرٌ and مَسْحُورٌ have competing Quranic interpretations: enchantment or delusion on one reading, and being a human endowed with bodily organs and needs on another.
سَحَرٌ as the pre-dawn time is distinct from the homonymous anatomical and deceptive branches of the root; inflection and context determine the intended branch.
